content.text:
**A:** You will not marry, if you have any sense at all, and you will not give up this life of yours. For I, who am speaking to you, did marry – that is why I advise you: do not take a wife!
**B:** The matter is decided and settled. Let the die be cast!
**A:** Very well, go. But may heaven let you come out of it safe.
You are now setting out on a true sea of troubles –
not the Libyan, not the Aegean, nor the Sicilian,
where of thirty ships three are saved –
no married man has ever been saved!

Caesar is only quoting Menander, but ==alea iacta est==: it is time to cross the Rubicon, or rather the Botič brook.

Choose a Caesar among you, who must cross the brook with dry feet, but not by the bridge.

**OR**

If the water is too cold for you, at least weave a laurel wreath out of leaves, which your chosen Caesar must wear until the end of the game.

Photos are welcome.
